data.name: Vietnamese Chicken Rice Porridge
data.description: Silky jasmine rice porridge meets tender poached chicken in a clear, savory broth, while fresh ginger, scallion whites, and bright green tops add crisp fragrance.

not_suitable_for: People with fish or anchovy allergies

refrigerator.notes: Cool the porridge and chicken promptly in shallow, covered containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C/39°F or below. Use within 3 days.

freezer.notes: Freeze in airtight portions for up to 1 month. Thaw in the refrigerator; the rice texture may become softer.

storage.reheating: Reheat only the portion needed, stirring until steaming throughout and the center reaches 74°C/165°F. Add a splash of hot water or broth if the porridge has thickened.

items.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
items.notes: Raw poultry. Keep separate from the cooked rice, vegetables, and garnishes.

items.name: cooked jasmine rice
items.notes: This is intentionally a cooked-weight measurement taken after steaming; it is not a dry-rice measurement.

items.name: water
items.notes: After poaching, strain the liquid and reserve 1,000 ml for the porridge; discard excess and sediment.

items.name: fresh ginger
items.notes: Divide into two 10 g portions, one for the poaching liquid and one for finishing.

items.name: scallions
items.notes: Use 20 g of the whites in the broth, 5 g of the greens in the finished porridge, and 5 g of the greens as garnish.

items.name: fish sauce
items.notes: Use 20 ml in the broth and 5 ml to finish the porridge.

instructions.text: Weigh 500 g of raw chicken thighs and 400 g of fully cooked, cooled jasmine rice. Keep the chicken and rice in separate containers until needed.

Cut the chicken into evenly sized 3 cm pieces. Use the cutting board and knife for the raw poultry at this stage, keep the chicken and its juices away from all other ingredients, and wash hands after handling it.

doneness_cues.visual: The pieces are approximately 3 cm across and similar in size.

instructions.text: Wash and sanitize the cutting board and knife, then mince the fresh ginger finely.

doneness_cues.visual: The ginger is finely minced with no large pieces remaining.

instructions.text: Slice the rinsed scallions thinly, placing 20 g of the whites, 5 g of the greens, and 5 g of the greens for garnish into separate piles.
Combine 1,200 ml of water with 20 ml of fish sauce, the sugar, salt, 10 g of minced ginger, and the 20 g of scallion whites in the saucepan.
Cover the saucepan and bring the seasoned liquid to a full boil over high heat, about 100°C/212°F.

doneness_cues.visual: Large bubbles rise rapidly across the surface.

instructions.text: Add the chicken, cover, and lower the heat to a gentle simmer at approximately 85-93°C/185-199°F. Poach for 12 minutes, then verify that the thickest piece reaches 74°C/165°F in the center; if necessary, continue in 2-minute increments and recheck.

doneness_cues.visual: The chicken is opaque throughout and the juices run clear.
doneness_cues.tactile: The thickest piece registers 74°C/165°F at its center.

tips: If the liquid boils vigorously, lower the heat immediately to prevent the chicken from toughening.

instructions.text: Lift the chicken from the saucepan with the tongs, place it in a clean heatproof bowl, and let it rest uncovered for 3 minutes.
Strain the poaching liquid through the fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, discarding foam and sediment. Reserve 1,000 ml of the strained liquid.

doneness_cues.visual: The liquid is clear without floating foam or sediment.

instructions.text: Shred the rested chicken with two forks, working with the grain and leaving the pieces slightly irregular for a tender, spoonable texture.

doneness_cues.visual: The chicken is separated into fine, moist strands without being overworked.

instructions.text: Add the 400 g of cooked jasmine rice and 1,000 ml of reserved broth to the saucepan. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, about 95°C/203°F.
Simmer the porridge uncovered for 12 minutes, stirring with the heatproof spoon every 3 minutes so the rice softens and releases its starch.

doneness_cues.visual: Most rice grains have softened and the porridge resembles loose cream.
doneness_cues.tactile: The mixture gently flows from the spoon while remaining slightly cohesive.

instructions.text: Reduce the heat and continue simmering for 5 minutes at approximately 94°C/201°F, stirring frequently until the porridge thickens and becomes creamy.

doneness_cues.visual: The porridge coats the spoon lightly and no thin liquid remains at the edges.
doneness_cues.tactile: The consistency is creamy but still able to flow.

instructions.text: Remove the porridge from the heat. Add the remaining 10 g of minced ginger, 5 g of scallion greens, remaining 5 ml of fish sauce, and black pepper, then stir to distribute them evenly.
Divide the shredded chicken among 4 serving bowls. Ladle over the hot porridge, scatter with the reserved scallion greens, and serve immediately.

troubleshooting.symptom: The porridge remains watery and runs off the spoon.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Too much broth was used, or the porridge was not reduced sufficiently.
troubleshooting.prevention: Measure the reserved broth accurately and simmer uncovered before reducing as directed.
troubleshooting.fix: Continue simmering over low heat, stirring frequently, until the porridge reaches a creamy consistency.

troubleshooting.symptom: The porridge has a scorched flavor or browned at the bottom.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The heat was too high or the porridge was not stirred often enough during reduction.
troubleshooting.prevention: Maintain a gentle simmer and stir from the bottom every few minutes.
troubleshooting.fix: Cannot be fixed if scorched; transfer the unaffected porridge to a clean saucepan and discard every scorched portion.

troubleshooting.symptom: The chicken is dry or tough after shredding.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The chicken may have simmered beyond the time needed to reach 74°C/165°F.
troubleshooting.prevention: Use evenly sized pieces and begin checking the thickest piece near the end of the poaching time.
troubleshooting.fix: Cannot fully restore tenderness; shred the chicken coarsely and moisten it with hot broth before serving.

troubleshooting.symptom: The center of a chicken piece measures below 74°C/165°F.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The pieces varied in thickness or the simmering heat was too gentle.
troubleshooting.prevention: Cut uniform 3 cm pieces and verify the temperature in the thickest piece.
troubleshooting.fix: Return the affected pieces to the simmering broth, cook in 2-minute increments, and recheck until they reach 74°C/165°F.

chef_notes: The 400 g rice quantity is intentionally measured after cooking so both the broth ratio and nutrition calculation use the same physical state.
Keep the heat gentle during both simmering and reduction; aggressive boiling can scorch the starch and make the chicken tough.
Check the thickest chicken piece rather than the liquid temperature because the required 74°C/165°F applies to the poultry itself.
For the smoothest texture, shred the chicken just before assembling and avoid grinding it into fine paste.
data.cultural_context: Cháo gà, literally chicken porridge, is a common Vietnamese home breakfast and comfort food in which rice is cooked until its starch gives the broth a soft, creamy body. Families vary the seasonings, but fresh ginger and scallions are classic accents that brighten the mild, savory dish.
